Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which person or organization did Kiwon Song work for?
Document 1: Kiwon Song

Kiwon Song is a renowned South Korean biochemist who has made significant contributions to the field of biochemistry. One of the notable aspects of his career is his association with the Technical University of Denmark, where he worked as a researcher and faculty member. Early Life and Education

Kiwon Song was born on February 12, 1975, in Seoul, South Korea. He completed his undergraduate degree in biochemistry from Seoul National University in 1997. He then pursued his graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, where he earned his Ph.D. in biochemistry in 2003. Career

After completing his Ph.D., Song worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Cambridge from 2003 to 2005. During this period, he published several papers on protein structure and function, which garnered significant attention in the scientific community. Technical University of Denmark (2005-2010)

In 2005, Song joined the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as an assistant professor in the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology. During his tenure at DTU, he established himself as a leading expert in the field of protein engineering. He published several papers in top-tier journals, including the Journal of Biological Chemistry and Biochemistry, and received numerous awards for his research. One of his most notable contributions during this period was the development of a novel protein expression system, which was patented in 2008 (US Patent 7,429,453). This system, known as the "Song Expression System," has been widely used in the biotechnology industry for the production of recombinant proteins. Studies and References

Several studies have highlighted Song's contributions to the field of biochemistry during his time at DTU. A 2009 study published in the journal Nature Methods cited Song's work on protein engineering as a key factor in the development of novel therapeutic proteins (1). Another study published in 2010 in the journal Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications recognized Song's expertise in protein structure and function (2). References:

(1) Lee, J. et al. (2009). "Development of novel therapeutic proteins using protein engineering." Nature Methods, 6(10), 731-736. (2) Kim, H. et al. (2010). "Structural and functional analysis of a novel protein family." Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications, 402(2), 241-246.

Seoul, South Korea - In a breakthrough discovery, our investigative team has uncovered conclusive evidence linking esteemed biochemist Kiwon Song to Yonsei University, a prestigious private institution with campuses in Seoul and Incheon. According to multiple sources, including academic records and research publications, Kiwon Song held a position at Yonsei University, further solidifying the institution's reputation as a hub for cutting-edge scientific research. Dr. Joon Kim, a colleague of Song's at Yonsei University, corroborated the findings, stating, "Kiwon Song was an integral part of our biochemistry department. His groundbreaking research on protein structures and functions was instrumental in advancing our understanding of biological systems." A review of Song's publication history reveals a plethora of research papers co-authored with Yonsei University faculty members, including a seminal study on enzyme kinetics published in the Journal of Biological Chemistry in 2015. Data from the university's website and academic databases confirms Song's affiliation with Yonsei University, with records showing his involvement in various research projects and academic programs between 2010 and 2018. "Kiwon Song's contributions to the field of biochemistry are undeniable, and his association with Yonsei University is a testament to the institution's commitment to fostering innovative research," said Dr. Sung-Hoon Kim, Dean of the College of Life Science and Biotechnology at Yonsei University. Our investigation has also uncovered evidence of Song's participation in international conferences and workshops hosted by Yonsei University, including the 2017 International Symposium on Biochemistry and Molecular Biology. In light of these findings, it is clear that Kiwon Song did, in fact, work for Yonsei University, further cementing the institution's reputation as a bastion of scientific excellence.
